title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Singapore top PISA education system
sections.summary: Singapore emerged as the top-performing education system for PISA last December, affirming the relevance and resilience of its education system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The relevance and resilience of our education system was affirmed when Singapore emerged as the top-performing education system for the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) last December.

sections.label: Expanding SkillsFuture Top-Up courses
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to consider expanding the courses and programmes the $4,000 SkillsFuture Top-Up can be used for, beyond local IHL programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In this regard, I urge the Ministry of Education (MOE) to consider expanding the suite of courses and programmes which the $4,000 SkillsFuture Top-Up can be used for, beyond programmes provided by our local Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), to programmes to uplift ability, agility and adaptability, including career design, career coaching and career counselling.

sections.label: Edusave top-up and student support
sections.summary: The passage welcomes a $2 billion Edusave Endowment Fund top-up and cites ITE upgrades, preschool fee reductions and childcare subsidy extensions as changes encouraging fairer opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It also recognises that each student learner experiences different starting points and that there is a need to actively support those with fewer educational resources and differing learning abilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the generous $2 billion top-up of the Edusave Endowment Fund, which will go a long way towards empowering students to achieve their aspirations and contribute to the well-being of others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I also commend the MOE's efforts to uplift and upgrade our Institute of Technical Education (ITE) graduates, something much overdue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The reduction of fees for Government-supported preschools and schools for children with special needs, as well as the extension of childcare subsidies to children of non-working mothers, are all changes that will encourage fairer opportunities for all students to attain social mobility.

sections.label: Extending SkillsFuture Credit validity
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOE will extend the validity of the $1,000 SkillsFuture credits to 2026 and let mature Singaporeans combine them with the latest tranche.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: CET modules, just as in mainstream, will therefore also need to diversify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am aware that the existing unused one-off SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 and additional credit for mid-career support of $500 is expiring in end-2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With the latest top up announced, will MOE consider extending the validity of this $1,000 for another year to 2026 and allow mature Singaporeans who have yet to utilise the credits an opportunity and more time to combine the $1,000 with the latest tranche to undertake the higher costs programmes.

sections.label: Full SBB rollout in schools
sections.summary: Full SBB was conducted in 28 secondary schools from 2020 and is being progressively rolled out to more secondary schools each year from 2022 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The establishment of SBB was part of MOE's aim to infuse joy of learning and to allow for multiple pathways to cater to the diverse strengths and interests of our students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that full SBB was conducted in 28 secondary schools from 2020, and progressively, it is being rolled out to more secondary schools each year from 2022 to 2024.

sections.label: Non-Tamil Indian languages examinations
sections.summary: In the early 1990s, the Government moved to allow Indian students to sit for five non-Tamil Indian languages at major examinations such as the O levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the early 1990s, the Government moved to allow Indian students to sit for five non-Tamil Indian languages, or NTILs, at major examinations, such as the "O" levels.

sections.label: MOE support for NTIL subjects
sections.summary: MOE supports Bengali, Urdu, Gujarati and Punjabi students through grants, weekend schools and community-provided teachers for national examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the main, MOE supports students taking these subjects, namely Bengali, Urdu, Gujarati and Punjabi, by way of grants and making available schools over the weekend, so that students sitting for national examinations in these subjects can receive an education in their mother tongue languages in a conducive environment, with teachers provided by the ethnic community groups.

sections.label: Hindi and Punjabi parallel programmes
sections.summary: Over 150 Hindi parallel programmes exist in MOE schools, while Punjabi has one school offering a parallel programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, by virtue of the large number of students taking Hindi, there are in excess of 150 parallel programmes for Hindi in MOE schools, while a smaller NTIL, for example, Punjabi, has one school offering a parallel programme.

sections.label: Grant framework and SBB implementation
sections.summary: The grant framework should be reviewed for small NTILs, and SBB is fully implemented for Secondary 1 in 120 secondary schools this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In theory, a "one-size-fits-all" grant is fair, but the unique challenge of each NTIL, particularly the small ones, should prompt a second look at the grant framework, so that the desired outcomes of the Ministry's bilingual policy are achieved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: This year, SBB has been fully implemented for the Secondary 1 cohort in 120 secondary schools across the island.

sections.label: SEC replacing O and N levels
sections.summary: From 2027, secondary students will receive the Singapore-Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate instead of the O or N levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: From 2027, secondary students will receive the Singapore-Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate (SEC), instead of the "O" or "N" levels.

sections.label: Pilot 10-year through-train programme
sections.summary: Last year, the speaker urged MOE to consider a pilot 10-year through-train programme letting students bypass the PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, last year, I urged MOE to consider implementing a pilot project of a 10-year through-train programme, giving students an option to bypass the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE).

sections.label: PSP urges through-train school pilot
sections.summary: The Progress Singapore Party urges the Government to pilot at least one through-train school in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Progress Singapore Party urges the Government to not hesitate with piloting at least one through-train school in Singapore.

sections.label: Transforming Education through Technology Masterplan 2030
sections.summary: Asks about the progress of the Transforming Education through Technology Masterplan 2030 and how the education system is being transformed for future needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: As such, what is the progress of the Transforming Education through Technology Masterplan 2030 and how are we transforming our education system to effectively meet the needs of the future?

sections.label: PLD programme for primary students
sections.summary: Asks MOE to consider a dedicated PLD programme for primary school students, similar to the secondary school one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that the Ministry has done a wonderful job by rolling out the PLD programme for the secondary school students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And with that framework already in place and the procurement process already familiar and the scheme to aid those students in secondary school who need financial assistance or PLDs already there, would MOE please consider also providing a dedicated PLD programme for primary school students – similar to the one that it has for secondary school students as well?

sections.label: AI education access inequality
sections.summary: States unequal access to AI education could worsen inequalities, so AI education should be in the national curriculum and teachers need professional development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unequal access to AI education could exacerbate existing inequalities, leaving some ill-prepared for an AI-driven world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is why we need to bridge this gap by making dedicated AI education a fundamental component of the national curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must also invest in more professional development for teachers to equip them with the skills to incorporate AI into the classrooms.

sections.label: Medical, assistive, therapy and transport costs
sections.summary: Lists medical expenses, assistive devices, therapies, transportation and caregiving arrangements as costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Generally, though, there would be medical expenses, cost for assistive devices, cost of therapies, transportation to get to and from medical appointments or therapies or caregiving arrangements.

sections.label: Higher salaries for SPED teachers
sections.summary: States the Ministry announced last year that teachers in SPED schools can expect higher salaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry announced that teachers in SPED schools can expect higher salaries.

sections.label: SPED and mainstream educator remuneration disparities
sections.summary: Asks whether planned salary increments would address disparities in remuneration and employment benefits between SPED and mainstream school educators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Currently, there are still disparities between the remuneration and employment benefits for the educators in the SPED schools and those in the mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Would the planned salary increments address these issues?

sections.label: SPED school funding from 2024
sections.summary: Additional funding for SPED schools was announced to be provided from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: To address these needs, it was announced that additional funding for SPED schools would be provided from 2024.

sections.label: SPED school fee reduction
sections.summary: The Government reduced the SPED school fee upper limit from $150 to $90, and a call was made to set fees at $13.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He felt that with the rising cost of living, a middle-income family like his should be eligible for a fee subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, Sir, I am glad that the Government has decided to reduce the upper limit of the SPED school fee from $150 to $90, announced in the Budget Statement as the first step in reducing the financial burden of families with special needs child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of this, I agree and fully support the call made by my fellow Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC) Member of Parliament, Mr Gerald Giam, through his Budget speech, asking the Government to set the fees for SPED schools at the same level as mainstream schools – namely $13 – on the basis of creating a more inclusive society.

sections.label: SEN officers in institutions
sections.summary: Polytechnics, ITE colleges and universities have only an average of three to four SEN officers across the whole institution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Polytechnics, ITE colleges and universities only have an average of three to four Special Educational Needs (SEN) officers across the whole institution.

sections.label: MOE SEN support improvements
sections.summary: MOE schools have made SEN improvements, and MOE was asked for data, challenges and partnership plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Improvements have been made in MOE schools over the past two decades, with the introduction of SEN offices, trained school teachers, learning support programmes and resource packages and a special education fund for tertiary-level students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Calls have been made for better equipping of teachers, SEN officers and parents through more skilling workshops, cluster-based parent support groups, communities of practice and to extend the SEN fund to postgraduate programmes for these students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I request the MOE to: one, provide updated data on the number of students with SEN, the support structure and SEN support staff strength at all education levels – primary school, secondary, junior college, ITE and other IHL levels; second, for MOE to share insights into the challenges it is facing in this space; and lastly, to share how it might partner key disability training groups, such as Dyslexia Association of Singapore, Unlocking ADHD, SPAS, Autism Resource Centre, Rainbow Centre and others in the Forward SG spirit to build a shared future together for this community.

sections.label: Redefining education in three parts
sections.summary: Education must be redefined as a continuing journey, celebrating diverse strengths, and a collective effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To stay ahead and prepare our next generation to learn for life, we must evolve our vision of education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We need to work with fellow Singaporeans, parents and industries to redefine success and redesign education in three parts: first, as a continuing journey, where we learn not just in the first 15 years, but throughout the next 50 years of our lives; second, to celebrate the diverse strengths, where we appreciate a diversity of talents for our collective resilience; and third, it must be a collective effort, where students learn not just in schools and from teachers, but from the community, society and even in the virtual world.

sections.label: Investing in people beyond school
sections.summary: There is time after formal schooling to discover strengths and purpose, and Singapore will invest in people over 50 years and beyond.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In the decades after formal schooling, there is time to discover new strengths and interests, to find our purpose and calling and to pursue them in different seasons of life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will continuously invest in our people to help them to do well not just for the first 15 years in school, but over the next 50 years and beyond.

sections.label: ITE diploma top-ups
sections.summary: ITE graduates enrolling in a diploma get a $5,000 PSEA top-up and $10,000 CPF Ordinary Account top-up on graduation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Upskilling to a diploma can help ITE graduates secure a better starting pay and a better lifetime earning trajectory through their improved skills and competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will hence top-up $5,000 to the Post-Secondary Education Accounts (PSEA) of ITE graduates when they enroll in a diploma programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When they graduate, they will receive a further $10,000 top-up to their CPF Ordinary Account.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit course fee help
sections.summary: An additional $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up provides more help with course fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, to provide more help with course fees through the additional SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $4,000.

sections.label: Subsidies for second diplomas
sections.summary: From 2025, Singaporeans aged 40 and above enrolling in a second full-time diploma will be subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: From 2025, we will subsidise Singaporeans aged 40 and above who enroll in a second full-time diploma.

sections.label: Training allowance for eligible individuals
sections.summary: Eligible individuals receive an allowance of 50% of average monthly income, capped at $3,000 for up to 24 months, up to $72,000 lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Eligible individuals will receive an allowance of 50% of their average monthly income over a year, capped at $3,000 for up to 24 months over their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In another words, up to $72,000 over a lifetime.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme cost
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme will cost the Government around an additional $100 million each year and more with stronger take-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme will cost the Government around an additional $100 million each year and more, if there is stronger take-up.

sections.label: New SEC examinations
sections.summary: In 2027, this year's Secondary 1 students sit new SEC examinations, replacing the GCE O and N level examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As the culmination of their Full SBB journey, in 2027, this year's Secondary 1 students will sit for a new Singapore-Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate (SEC) examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The SEC examinations will replace the current Singapore-Cambridge General Certificate of Education (GCE) "O" and "N" level examinations.

sections.label: Second sitting posting outcomes
sections.summary: Taking a second sitting changed post-secondary posting outcomes for less than 2% of students taking the examination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our analysis shows that taking a second sitting only changed the post-secondary posting outcomes for less than 2% of the students taking the examination.

sections.label: ELR2B2 Best subject grade
sections.summary: From 2028, one Best or B subject in the ELR2B2 score may be taken at G2 or G3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: From 2028, we will allow one of the "Best" or "B" subjects in the ELR2B2 score to be taken at either G2 or G3.

sections.label: 21st Century Competencies and Edusave awards
sections.summary: Students need 21st Century Competencies like civic literacy and adaptive thinking, so the balance of academic and non-academic Edusave awards will be improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We also need to equip our students with "21st Century Competencies" (21CC), like civic literacy and adaptive thinking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Hence, we will improve the balance of academic and non-academic Edusave awards.

sections.label: Additional students receiving Edusave awards
sections.summary: An additional 21,000 students could receive an award yearly, bringing academic and non-academic awards to around 60:40 from around 70:30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With this, an additional 21,000 students could receive an award every year, bringing the balance of academic and non-academic awards given out to around 60:40, down from around 70:30 ratio.

sections.label: Reducing fees in SPED schools
sections.summary: School fees in nine higher-fee SPED schools will be reduced to alleviate pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As announced at Budget, we will alleviate these pressures by reducing school fees in nine higher-fee SPED schools.

sections.label: Industry partners collaborating with schools
sections.summary: Over 150 industry partners came forward through MOE's Partnerships Engagement Office to collaborate with schools and create authentic learning opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, the over 150 industry partners who have come forward through MOE's Partnerships Engagement Office to collaborate with our schools, to create authentic learning opportunities for our students.

sections.label: EdTech and adaptive learning investment
sections.summary: Technology will be the multiplier of teachers' capacity, with continued investment in EdTech and adaptive learning systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Technology must increasingly be the multiplier of our teachers' capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will continue investing in EdTech and adaptive learning systems, to help our teachers support those who need more help, while stretching those who can do more.

sections.label: Teachers as coaches and mentors
sections.summary: Teachers will play bigger roles as coaches and mentors, with commitment to their professional and personal growth, and trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: They will play a bigger role as coaches and mentors, guiding students in developing softer skills and navigating complex issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will hence be committed to making time for our teachers' growth professionally to learn new pedagogies and skill sets, but also personally to spend time away from the classroom and gain exposure and new perspectives so that they can broaden their minds, refresh themselves and bring back ideas to share with their students and fellow colleagues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But the last T is most critical, and that is trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We must maintain our trust and support in our educators.

sections.label: Children's growth over grades
sections.summary: Together, we can show our children that their growth matters more than their grades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Together, we can show our children that their growth matters more than their grades.

sections.label: MOE delivering for children
sections.summary: MOE and partners are committed to delivering this for our children and our nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE and our partners are committed to delivering this for our children and our nation.

sections.label: Clarify programme choice and vacancies
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to clarify how programmes or courses are chosen, company readiness, and job market vacancies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry clarify how the programmes or courses are chosen, whether companies are ready to take in these graduates and whether there are enough vacancies in the job market for them to transit to or join as graduates in a new field?

sections.label: Assessing SkillsFuture effectiveness
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how it will assess the effectiveness of the SkillsFuture movement, including social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In view of this, my questions are: how will the Ministry assess the effectiveness of the SkillsFuture movement, including with respect to strengthening the social mobility of Singaporeans?

sections.label: Training allowance and part-time work
sections.summary: The new monthly training allowance of up to $3,000 for up to 24 months may not suffice for mature students with financial commitments, so the Ministry is asked if they can take part-time work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The newly announced monthly training allowance of up to $3,000 for up to 24 months will be useful to mitigate the loss of income during their training period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: Given that the allowance may still not be enough for some mature students with significant financial commitments, I would like to ask the Ministry if these students could still take on part-time work during their training to supplement their income?

sections.label: Sector-specific SkillsFuture training demand
sections.summary: The business sector suggests more specialised, sector-specific SkillsFuture training, citing manufacturing demand for AI and sustainability reporting courses, and asks about plans to enhance such opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the business sector would like to suggest more specialised, sector-specific training for SkillsFuture to meet industry's needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is particularly evident in the manufacturing sector where there is a significant demand for courses in areas, like artificial intelligence (AI) in manufacturing and sustainability reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of these industry demands, could the Ministry share any plans to enhance the SkillsFuture programme with more in-depth, sector-specific training opportunities?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme welcomed
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, including SkillsFuture Credit for mid-career Singaporeans' full-time diplomas and training allowances, has been welcomed by almost all quarters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, which includes the SkillsFuture Credit, giving mid-career Singaporeans a second shot at a subsidy for publicly funded full-time diplomas and the training allowances, have been welcomed by almost all quarters.

sections.label: Outcome metrics and industry-linked providers
sections.summary: The Government should track outcome metrics such as placement into roles using acquired skills, and nurture industry-linked training providers for working adults, with the speaker declaring interest as CEO of the Wealth Management Institute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government will need to track the right metrics, which are not so much the percentage shake-up but the outcome metrics, such as placement into roles that use the skills acquired.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, I declare my interest as the Chief Executive Officer of the Wealth Management Institute, a training provider serving the finance sector with programmes eligible for SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: But I urge the Government to nurture a new generation of industry-linked training providers, specially designed to serve the unique learning needs of working adults.

sections.label: SkillsFuture quality accreditation framework
sections.summary: The Government could introduce a SkillsFuture quality accreditation framework with a differentiated funding model based on curriculum relevance, qualified trainers, industry involvement and employment outcomes, giving proven industry-linked providers support comparable to publicly funded IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the development of this new ecosystem, the Government can assume a pivotal role by introducing a SkillsFuture quality accreditation framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This framework could implement a differentiated funding model, based on several key factors: the curriculum's relevance to practice, the involvement of qualified industry trainers and instructors, industry and employer involvement and endorsement as well as employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Industry-linked training providers that have a proven track record of delivering strong outcomes should, over time, receive support and recognition comparable to that accorded to publicly funded IHLs.

sections.label: Extending programme to younger Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to extend or contextualise the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme and ITE Progression Award to Singaporeans in their 30s, and extend SkillsFuture Credit to workers below age 25.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, could the Ministry extend, or as a baseline, contextualise the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme and the ITE Progression Award to Singaporeans in their 30s who need a boost to their career health and, in the same vein, extend the SkillsFuture Credit to Singaporean workers below age 25?

sections.label: SkillsFuture grant for freelancers
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-up $4,000 grant applies to courses with better employability outcomes, and the Ministry is asked to clarify how it benefits freelancers and self-employed persons, many in the arts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the newly announced SkillsFuture Level-up $4,000 grant will be applicable to courses with "better employability outcomes." Would the Ministry be able to clarify how exactly the grant will benefit freelancers and self-employed persons (SEPs), a large proportion of whom work in the arts?

sections.label: Training allowance income basis
sections.summary: The training allowance announced in the Budget Statement is capped at $3,000 and based on a person's average income earned in the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My second point has to do with the training allowance that has been announced in the Budget Statement, capped at $3,000, and which is based on a person's average income earned in the previous year.

sections.label: Training allowance and course eligibility
sections.summary: MOE is asked whether the training allowance can be based on last-drawn full-time income instead of the previous year's income, and how it will decide which of over 29,000 SkillsFuture courses are eligible for the $4,000 top-up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOE consider basing the training allowance on the last-drawn full-time income instead of the previous year's income?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I applaud the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, which provides $4,000 top-up for Singaporeans aged 40 and above, subsidies to the second publicly funded diploma or publicly subsidised diploma, and the ITE Progression Award.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that there are over 29,000 courses on the SkillsFuture website, how will the Ministry decide which training programmes will be eligible for this top-up funding?

sections.label: Preventing inflated training fees
sections.summary: The question asks how to prevent over-inflated training fees to prevent excessive claims by training vendors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How do we prevent over-inflated training fees to prevent excessive claims by training vendors?

sections.label: SkillsFuture access for PwDs
sections.summary: The Government is asked how it can collaborate with continuing education and training centres to ensure SkillsFuture courses eligible for the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme are accessible to persons with disabilities, particularly those with visual impairments or neuro-diverse needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In light of this, what are the ways the Government can collaborate with continuing education and training (CET) centres to ensure that SkillsFuture courses eligible for the newly introduced SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme are accessible to PwDs, particularly those with visual impairments or neuro-diverse needs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Chairman, I commend MOE's efforts for its dedication to lifelong learning in Budget 2024, focusing on younger ITE graduates and mid-career Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I seek MOE's response to what I raised in my Budget speech on the challenges these groups face, such as opportunity costs or income loss, and also ensuring positive job outcomes from further education.

sections.label: MOE study on lifelong learning
sections.summary: MOE is urged to commission a comprehensive study to map the current landscape for lifelong learning for all, analyse disability profiles and assess learning needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a leader in education and with the Minister championing lifelong learning for all Singaporeans, MOE is positioned to spearhead this domain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is a pressing need for MOE to commission a comprehensive study to map the current landscape for lifelong learning for all, analyse disability profiles and assess learning needs.

sections.label: ITE graduates further education diplomas
sections.summary: The passage asks what range of diploma programmes the initiative encouraging ITE graduates aged 30 and below to pursue further education covers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Chairman, in an economy that is increasingly valuing diverse skills and lifelong learning, the move to encourage our ITE graduates, especially those aged 30 and below, to pursue further education and skills enhancement is very timely.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: This brings us to an important question: what is the range of diploma programmes that this initiative covers?

sections.label: Financial support for ITE graduates
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would expand scholarships and grants so programmes are accessible to all ITE graduates wishing to further their education.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Additionally, would the Ministry expand financial support mechanisms, such as scholarships and grants, to ensure these programmes are accessible to all ITE graduates who wish to further their education?

sections.label: ITE Progression Award diplomas
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will introduce the ITE Progression Award, which diplomas apply, and whether independent school diplomas qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, how will the Ministry intend to introduce the ITE Progression Award?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: What are the types of diplomas that will be applicable for this award that is in line with the needs of the industry?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Will it be applicable for diplomas from independent schools?

sections.label: Encouragement and WSDip university progression
sections.summary: The passage states graduates need encouragement to find a suitable field and asks how many WSDip graduates went on to university.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: They need more encouragement to help them find a suitable field to excel in and they should not be compelled to start work and concurrently study when they are ill-prepared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And of those who have graduated with the WSDip, how many went on to university?

sections.label: PSGs, COMPASS and parental involvement
sections.summary: The passage requests an update on PSG progress, COMPASS advisory panel role, and strategies for harnessing parents' energy to strengthen education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: This may help to enhance the cascading of critical information and resources more effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I request an update from MOE on the progress of PSGs over the years, the role of the Community and Parents in Support of Schools (COMPASS) advisory panel and strategies for harnessing parents' energy to strengthen our education system as a whole.

sections.label: Parental involvement and mental health support
sections.summary: The passage asks what MOE initiatives enhance parental involvement in holistic development and whether platforms or PSG mental health partnerships would be considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, a pivotal question arises: what initiatives are MOE implementing to enhance parental involvement and collaboration in supporting our students' holistic development, for example, in areas like mental well-being?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider establishing a co-curated dedicated platform or portal centralising resources, research and expert advice on children's mental health?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Could the Ministry explore partnerships between PSGs and mental health professionals, to conduct regular webinars and workshops for parents and educators?

sections.label: KCare subsidy extension
sections.summary: MOE extends KCare subsidies to all families earning up to $6,000 monthly from the fourth quarter this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam will be pleased to know that MOE will extend the KCare AS to all families, that is, regardless of their mother's working status and earning up to $6,000 per month from the fourth quarter this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This means all families with a gross monthly household income of up to $6,000 will receive subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Those with a gross monthly household income of $3,000 and below will pay as low as $3 a month for MK and KCare.

sections.label: UPLIFT student support 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, UPLIFT supported about 16,500 students in around 300 schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2023, UPLIFT supported about 16,500 students in around 300 schools.

sections.label: SEN students in mainstream schools
sections.summary: About 28,500 SEN students, or about 80% of all SEN students, attend mainstream schools and receive targeted help.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: About 28,500 SEN students, or about 80% of all SEN students, attend mainstream schools today, and receive targeted help.

sections.label: SPED school fee reductions
sections.summary: Fees for Singapore Citizens in SPED schools were reduced from $350 to $150, and will fall to $90 by mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2023, we worked with social service agencies (SSAs) to reduce maximum fees for Singapore Citizens in SPED schools from $350 to $150.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As outlined in the Budget Statement, we have worked with nine higher-fee SPED schools serving students with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Multiple Disabilities to lower their fees by up to 60% for Singapore Citizens by mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With this, the maximum monthly fees for any Singapore Citizen in SPED schools will be reduced from $150 to $90.

sections.label: SPED teacher salary enhancements
sections.summary: Between 2024 and 2026, existing trained SPED classroom teachers can see salary enhancements of up to 12%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Between 2024 and 2026, existing trained SPED classroom teachers can see salary enhancements of up to 12%.

sections.label: G2 subject polytechnic admission
sections.summary: From 2028, students may use one B subject at G2 for admission to polytechnic Year 1.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: From 2028, students may use one B subject at G2 for admission to polytechnic Year 1.

sections.label: Polytechnic Year 1 cut-off adjustment
sections.summary: The net aggregate cut-off for Year 1 polytechnic admission will be adjusted from 26 points to 22 points.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: With this, the net aggregate cut-off for Year 1 polytechnic admission will be adjusted from 26 points to 22 points.

sections.label: ITE Progression Award funding
sections.summary: MOE will set aside around $100 million annually for the ITE Progression Award and support Singaporean ITE graduates aged 30 and below.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: MOE will set aside around $100 million annually for the ITE Progression Award (IPA) and support Singaporean ITE graduates aged 30 and below on their upgrading journeys.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: On diploma enrolment, ITE graduates will receive a $5,000 top-up to their Post-Secondary Education Accounts (PSEA).

sections.label: Sustainability initiative at polytechnics and ITE
sections.summary: Polytechnics and ITE will pilot a sustainability initiative where students adopt three blocks near their campuses and engage residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Beyond learning about sustainability concepts in class, polytechnics and ITE will pilot a new sustainability initiative this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Students from each institution will "adopt" three blocks near their campuses and engage residents through workshops and visits to reduce water consumption and electricity consumption and increase recycling and greening efforts.

sections.label: Mother Tongue Language committees spending
sections.summary: The Mother Tongue Language Learning and Promotion Committees spend around $5 million annually to promote Mother Tongue Languages learning and usage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The Mother Tongue Language Learning and Promotion Committees (MTLLPCs) spend around $5 million annually to promote Mother Tongue Languages learning and usage.

sections.label: Full SBB polytechnic access
sections.summary: In line with Full Subject-Based Banding in secondary schools, wider profiles of learners will gain access to polytechnic Year 1 from 2028.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: In line with the Full Subject-Based Banding (SBB) in secondary schools, wider profiles of learners will gain access to polytechnic Year 1 from 2028.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Singapore training beneficiaries
sections.summary: Last year, more than 500,000 individuals benefitted from training supported by SkillsFuture Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Last year, more than 500,000 individuals benefitted from training supported by SkillsFuture Singapore.

sections.label: Curated courses across sectors
sections.summary: Over 7,000 courses have been curated, covering a range of sectors and job profiles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: For a start, we have curated over 7,000 courses, covering a good range of sectors and job profiles.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up for Ms Low
sections.summary: The $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up would cover at least half of Ms Low's full-time course fees, plus a training allowance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: If Ms Low decides to further deepen her skills in a few years’ time and enrol in a full-time course, for example, a diploma in sustainability, the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up will be sufficient to cover at least half her course fees and she will also get training allowance amounting to 50% of her last drawn salary, up to $3,000 per month.

sections.label: Companies in SSG programmes
sections.summary: In 2023, around 23,000 companies participated in SSG-supported programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2023, around 23,000 companies participated in SSG-supported programmes.

sections.label: Skills Profiler pilot for SMEs
sections.summary: The Skills Profiler pilot went to 400 SMEs last year, and SSG will make it available to 1,000 more enterprises this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Skills Profiler pilot was rolled out to 400 SMEs last year, with all slots snapped up within seven months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To support more SMEs in conducting training needs analyses, SSG will make the Skills Profiler available to 1,000 more enterprises this year.

sections.label: SFEC extension and tax deduction
sections.summary: MTI announced the SFEC is extended to June 2025, and corporate tax deduction for training is enhanced from 100% to 400%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: MTI has announced that the SFEC has been extended to June 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: And beginning from Year of Assessment 2024, corporate tax deduction for training has been enhanced from 100% to 400% under the Enterprise Innovation Scheme.

sections.label: PSG Support Circles from 2024
sections.summary: From 2024, every PSG will be part of a Support Circle to share resources and ideas across schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We recognise that each PSG has unique yet useful experiences that other PSGs can learn from.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Therefore, to encourage sharing of learnings across PSGs, every PSG will be part of a Support Circle from 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Support Circles are communities of PSGs across various schools where they can share resources and ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: They can decide on the topics to collaborate on, such as supporting parents of children with special educational needs (SEN) and strengthening our students' mental well-being.

sections.label: CCE Israel-Hamas lesson aims
sections.summary: The CCE lesson aims to help students understand the conflict, appreciate diverse perspectives, discern information and support social cohesion, without imposing any perspective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In the case of the CCE lesson on the Israel-Hamas conflict, our aims are for students to (i) help them understand what is going on, express their own views and manage their own emotions; (ii) appreciate diverse perspectives sensitively and respectfully; (iii) discern information from different sources; and (iv) play their part to support racial harmony and social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It does not tell students that one party in this conflict is good and the other is evil.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It does not impose any particular perspective or interpretation of events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It most certainly does not create a wedge between our students' religious beliefs and their national identity.

sections.label: Updating CCE materials
sections.summary: Materials will be updated to address feedback and ongoing developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As I shared with the media last week, we will update our materials to address the feedback and ongoing developments.

sections.label: Gaza humanitarian ceasefire call
sections.summary: The catastrophic situation in Gaza demands a humanitarian ceasefire to alleviate civilian suffering and enable immediate humanitarian assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The catastrophic situation in Gaza demands a humanitarian ceasefire to alleviate the suffering of the civilian victims and to enable humanitarian assistance to reach them immediately.

sections.label: Singapore Centre for CCE
sections.summary: The Singapore Centre for CCE was set up at the National Institute of Education to support professional development of CCE educators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Last May, we set up the Singapore Centre for CCE at the National Institute of Education to support professional development of educators in CCE.

sections.label: Slide wording and accusation
sections.summary: It was insinuated that MOE was pro-Israel, but the slide said "events since 7 October" after one on the region's long, complex, violent history.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This insinuated that MOE was pro-Israel and that we characterised one side as the aggressor and the other side as victim.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This riled up many but actually, the words on the said slide were "events since 7 October", and it came after a slide that emphasised the long, complex and often violent history of conflict in the region.

sections.label: Protection for educators
sections.summary: MOE will investigate all abuse, harassment or threats against educators, who have MOE's full support and the law's full protection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MOE will investigate all instances of abuse, harassment or threats against our educators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They have MOE's full support and the full protection of the law.

sections.label: Meeting school principals again
sections.summary: The Second Minister and the speaker met more than 300 school principals again to hear their feedback since January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Last week, Second Minister Maliki Osman and I met more than 300 school principals again to listen to their feedback since we last discussed the issue with them in January.

sections.label: Debate on continuing CCE lesson
sections.summary: In light of criticisms against schools and teachers, they discussed whether to continue teaching the CCE lesson despite suggestions to abandon it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In the light of this episode and criticisms against our schools and teachers, we discussed frankly, should we continue teaching this CCE lesson, given that some people have suggested that we should abandon it since it is so difficult and sensitive?

sections.label: Starting scheme with ITE students
sections.summary: The answer is yes; they will start the scheme first, gain experience, and focus finite resources on ITE students who need it most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The answer to the first question is, yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At this point in time, I think let us get the scheme started first and get some experience doing this, and focus our finite resources on the group that need it most, which is the ITE students.

sections.label: Goal for polytechnic students
sections.summary: The goal is to ensure students who qualify for the polytechnic have the capabilities and capacities to finish the course well, starting with one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our goal is to make sure that the students who qualify for the polytechnic has the capabilities and the capacities to finish the course and do it well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And at this point in time, we start with one.

sections.label: No increase in 2022 review
sections.summary: For Mr Pritam Singh's first question, it was not increased in the 2022 review because it was still commensurate with needs of supporting NTIL students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: For Mr Pritam Singh's first question, I think the Member's question is: when we reviewed it in 2022, whether it was increased or not.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: It was not increased because we felt it was still commensurate with the needs of providing the support for the students who are taking the NTIL lessons.

sections.label: No devices for all upper primary
sections.summary: Their conclusion is that, as a general policy, they will not want to issue the devices to every upper primary school student yet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our conclusion at this point in time is that, as a general policy, we will not want to issue the devices to every upper primary school student yet.

sections.label: Device use and sharing
sections.summary: The passage states the need to guide youngest students in responsible device use and that upper primary students share devices in school rather than own them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We need to strengthen how we guide our youngest students to use the devices responsibly so that we do not get into the ills of using those devices inadvertently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But having said that, what we have done is that instead of issuing every upper primary school student with the device, we have increased the provision of the devices in the school so that for more classes, they can use the devices and to share the devices rather than to own it themselves.

sections.label: Maximum monthly fee reduced
sections.summary: The passage states yearly review of support and that the maximum monthly fee has been brought down to $90 this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: And that is the reason why we continue to review, on a yearly basis, how we can continue to support them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: This year we have announced that we have brought down the maximum monthly fee to $90.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We agree that the gap is still wide and 50% are already paying similar fees.

sections.label: Special needs student assessment
sections.summary: The passage states students' conditions are assessed for mainstream versus SPED school, and that 80% are in mainstream school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: And many of those who are keen in the special needs sector also understand that we have to assess the students' conditions and whether they will be able to harness their potential to the fullest when they are in mainstream school vis-à-vis in the SPED school.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: So, 80% are in the mainstream school and we will assess such that we try to integrate them as much as possible.

sections.label: SSG partners and SkillsFuture courses
sections.summary: The passage states SSG is guided by partners and job transformation maps in deciding courses, and invites notification of additional needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Indeed, SSG stands guided by the partners that we work with, whether it is NTUC, the professional bodies or trade associations and yes, job transformation maps do also feature in how we decide on which courses we need to provide upskilling opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: If Ms Jean See knows of freelancers or self-employed persons who have additional needs that are not already catered in the range of causes supported by SkillsFuture, do let us know and we will consider them too.

sections.label: Release of teaching materials
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOE can release teaching materials or slides to the public to stop false news being shared online.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: In the interest of transparency, can the MOE release the teaching materials or the right slides that were used, to the public, so that we can make sure that the false news is not being shared online further.

sections.label: Quality of teachers
sections.summary: The passage states that if one reason is chosen for why an education system works, it is the quality of the teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If there is one reason and only one reason that we choose as to why an education system works or not work, it is the quality of the teachers.

sections.label: Respect for teachers
sections.summary: The speaker says respect for teachers is the most important support, and discussed with MOE colleagues whether to publish MOE slides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Is it because of the infrastructure that we provide for them, the lesson material?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But just as the OECD report has highlighted, ultimately, the most important support that we can give our teachers and attract the best and most committed people to join the teaching service in service of our future generation is the respect that we give to our teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On Dr Wan Rizal's point, I also discussed this extensively with my colleagues in MOE whether we should just publish the MOE slides.

sections.label: PSLE compulsory and scores
sections.summary: The question asks whether making PSLE compulsory and using scores for secondary school reinforces that worth is defined by examination results.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Does the Minister not agree that if we insist on making the PSLE compulsory and using the scores as a basis for deciding secondary school, then that reinforces the idea that our worth is defined by examination results?

sections.label: MOE considering implications
sections.summary: The speaker says questions raised remain and MOE is carefully considering all these before making a decision with serious implications for students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But every idea also has implications that we need to step through and those questions that I have raised and shared with this House remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why MOE is carefully considering all these before we make such an important decision with serious implications for the students that will have to undergo this system.

sections.label: Direct School Admissions expansion
sections.summary: The speaker says challenges exist in one system and the Direct School Admissions system has been expanded to allow abilities beyond academic success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We already have challenges doing this in one system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And indeed, over time, we have expanded the Direct School Admissions (DSA) system to allow more dimensions of abilities beyond academic success.

sections.label: Teachers facilitating discussions
sections.summary: The question asks how to check that teachers are ready to facilitate such discussions without imposing their own opinions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: How do we check that our teachers are ready to facilitate such discussions without imposing their own opinions on the matter?

sections.label: Pausing lessons
sections.summary: The question asks whether lessons will be paused as these changes are dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Thirdly, as we deal with these changes, will we be pausing the lessons?

sections.label: Palestine materials and teacher training
sections.summary: The record on Palestine issues will be part of materials, with slides being updated and further teacher training conducted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, indeed, I have said in my reply that our record on the Palestine issues will be as part of the materials, but we are careful not to inundate the younger students with all the history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Third, we are now in the process of updating the slides and also conducting further training with our teachers as we go along and this is our promise to everyone, that we will continue to do this as we go along.

sections.label: Threats to teachers
sections.summary: The speaker will deal with backlash from members of the public who make threats to teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Fourth point: I will deal with the backlash from some of the public who make threats to our teachers.

sections.label: Consulting parents on CCE lessons
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MOE considered consulting parents of younger students about the sensitive CCE lesson.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I heard Minister acknowledging that the issue of the Israel-Palestine conflict is a sensitive one a few times in his speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I just want to know whether MOE considered in the first place, to consult parents of younger students whether they are comfortable to have their children partake in this particular CCE lesson, which touches on sensitive issues, like what Minister said?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Chair, I would like to make a distinction between sexuality education and CCE lessons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For CCE issues, we are talking about people relating to one another respectfully and sensitively.

sections.label: Students and information bombardment
sections.summary: The question asks how students are helped with emotions and distinguishing news, fake news and misinformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: How do we help our students deal with their emotions when they are being bombarded by information all around, how to distinguish news, fake news, misinformation and others?

sections.label: Shared values and common future
sections.summary: The vision is to understand the past deeply while having shared values that unite Singaporeans going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Neither is our vision one whereby we all cling on to our past and have no common future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want the best of both worlds where we deeply understand our past and yet at the same time have a set of shared values, a set of ethos that can bring us forward together as Singaporeans, united as one.
